officialTitle: Prophylactic cranial irradiation in extensive small-cell lung cancer
setting: Extensive-stage SCLC responding to first-line chemotherapy

design.notes: Brain imaging was performed only when predefined symptoms suggested brain metastases; no mandatory baseline brain MRI. Each arm included 143 patients.

clinicalQuestion: In extensive-stage SCLC responding to chemotherapy, does prophylactic cranial irradiation reduce symptomatic brain metastases and improve survival?

pico.population: Patients aged 18-75 years with extensive SCLC responding to chemotherapy
pico.outcomes: Primary: time to symptomatic brain metastases. Secondary: DFS, OS, global health status

publications.title: Prophylactic cranial irradiation in extensive small-cell lung cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Patients in the irradiation group had a lower risk of symptomatic brain metastases (hazard ratio, 0.27; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.16 to 0.44; P<0.001). The cumulative risk of brain metastases within 1 year was 14.6% in the irradiation group (95% CI, 8.3 to 20.9) and 40.4% in the control group (95% CI, 32.1 to 48.6).

Irradiation was associated with an increase in median disease-free survival from 12.0 weeks to 14.7 weeks and in median overall survival from 5.4 months to 6.7 months after randomization. The 1-year survival rate was 27.1% (95% CI, 19.4 to 35.5) in the irradiation group and 13.3% (95% CI, 8.1 to 19.9) in the control group.

safety.description: PCI had side effects but no clinically significant effect on global health status (no numbers in abstract)
safety.sourceQuote: Irradiation had side effects but did not have a clinically significant effect on global health status.

strengths: Clear reduction in symptomatic brain metastases
limitations: No mandatory brain imaging before randomisation, so some patients may have had asymptomatic brain metastases at entry
Brain imaging only when symptomatic during follow-up
Chemotherapy regimens and PCI dose schedules were not uniform

clinicalImplications.text: Supported PCI after response to chemotherapy in extensive-stage SCLC in the era before routine MRI staging; its applicability has been questioned by the later Japanese MRI-surveillance trial.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Ask whether the patient had a baseline brain MRI: this trial did not require one, which is the key difference from the Japanese trial that found no survival benefit with MRI surveillance.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 17699816. The abstract reports no OS hazard ratio or P value.
